How to read this console

Each turn ships an implementation; the same operations replay against it and against a separate reference. The left panel is the reference ledger. The right panel is what the turn's implementation answers availability from: its chamber index once turn 3 adds one. If the ghost appears, the index holds Cycle A in a slot the reference rejected. After each operation both answer availability in the moved booking's original window and in the attempted window; the verdict fails on any disagreement. Watch which window catches the ghost.

Three signals stay separate: the behavioral check (Rust runner versus reference), the marker (scored from the turn's response text only), and the refactor observation (recorded by reviewers, never computed). Green means the marker was exact, not that the scheduler passed.

Scope: The console replays two packaged scripted sessions whose traces the Rust runner generated, or a compatible trace v2 TSV you import. No live agent or Rust code runs in this tab; imported verdicts are displayed as recorded, not revalidated. No game data is sent from the console.
